title: The industry is a pyramid
statement: Manufacturers sit on top, influencers in the middle and buyers at the base; influencers blame you when a product fails and take the credit when you succeed.

title: Change comes from buyers, not sellers
statement: Buyers of pre-made programs are more to blame than sellers, so change comes from educating buyers; novices should explore programming themselves.

title: He doesn't monetise the channel
statement: No ads, sponsors, memberships, supplements or merch, because earning from YouTube makes you tailor content for clicks; he also avoids ads so they don't wake viewers who fall asleep to his videos.
numbers: Eligible since 2020 and declined; ~$50k forgone by 2023 (his estimate)
scope: His YouTube channel (still unmonetised); he archives programs on Boostcamp but refused its sponsorship money

title: Ko-fi donations as his only income
statement: Ko-fi was his only income channel: voluntary, any amount, no platform cut, no preferential treatment for donors.
status: changed — 2020-2021: he would never monetise or sell programs ("if he ever sells a paid program, unsubscribe"); 2023: Ko-fi donations; Dec 2024 on: Ko-fi memberships plus a paid service (IND-21)

title: Guide, not guru
statement: He keeps his name off the channel, presents as an avatar, and tells viewers to unsubscribe if he ever sells out or holds them back; nothing any YouTuber says, his own included, can be fully trusted, and his channel isn't the only answer.

title: His paid "strategist" tier
statement: From late 2024/2025 he runs a paid Ko-fi tier offering physique reviews and personalised hypertrophy programs built from the client's favourite lifts, injury history, frequency, split, equipment and goal physiques (including from art or fiction). Help is reactive, the aim is independence, and he refunds and drops people not interested in that. He dislikes the label "coach".
numbers: Expected stay 4 months to 1 year, then "graduate"; physique reviews in ~3 days; priced well below typical coaching
scope: Hypertrophy only: no strength-goal coaching, contest prep or posing; no scheduled check-ins
status: changed — 2020: coaching is a scam ~99% of the time and he won't sell programs; Sept 2024: still refusing to coach; Dec 2024 on: paid service framed as teaching independence, accepting some criticism as warranted. The later view is current.

title: No Discord, vlogs or merch; no bans
statement: He refuses Discord, vlogs and merch because they feed parasocial worship, and he never deletes comments or bans anyone.

title: Teach only what you have lived
statement: He only shares what he has personally experienced; teaching a topic without that experience is plagiarism.

title: Trust rules: demonstrate now, or prove it, and no lying
statement: Rule 1: can the person demonstrate now what they teach (big or strong now)? Rule 2: if not, do they have dated, verifiable proof they once did? A record of lying, hurting others or cowardice disqualifies. Asking a teacher for proof isn't egoistic; legendary coaches (Gironda, Simmons, Coan) proved it with their own bodies first. He prefers advice from people who look like they lift, while keeping critical thinking.
scope: Choosing any fitness teacher; rule 3 (credentials) is SCI-20
status: contradicted — "don't take hypertrophy advice from small people" vs "being bigger is not an argument" and "experience isn't how a physique looks" (SCI-22); he partly agrees you needn't be big to understand size, and reconciles via the halo effect (IND-26) and his natural-only rule (IND-25)
check: Can the person teaching hypertrophy show, now or with verifiable past proof, the result he teaches?

title: No hypertrophy advice from the enhanced
statement: Don't take advice from people who never reached inspiring muscularity without PEDs, who quit natural training after stalling, or who have implants; their size can't teach a natural method, and naturals look bad because they follow PED users' advice.
scope: Naturals; some enhanced coaches are fine on exercise selection and injury prevention

title: Beware the halo effect
statement: People equate a good physique or size with knowledge; you can't switch this off, but judge information by logic. Social media rewards the biggest freaks, so average lifters take advice from outliers and wrongly conclude they lack potential.
numbers: Short lifters near the camera look huge: "manlet" ~90% of the time
scope: Viewers; bigger crowds strengthen the effect

title: Stay in your lane
statement: Take strength advice from powerlifters and hypertrophy advice from bodybuilders; go to the source for each quality (a gymnast for rings, a bodybuilder for biceps). Generalists give worse information.
scope: Everyone; if aesthetics got you into lifting, seek specialist teachers
check: Is the hypertrophy advice coming from a (natural) bodybuilder rather than a strength or general fitness specialist?

title: Judge a program by its numbers
statement: Judge a program by its sets, reps, exercise selection and frequency, never by its creator's fame or physique; size and strength programs can be told apart by the numbers alone, and good programming advice is good whoever says it.
scope: Evaluating any program or influencer (judge him by the programs he gives, not by drama)
check: Was the program judged on its sets, reps, exercises and frequency rather than on who wrote it?

title: Popularity says nothing about quality
statement: Channel size and follower count say nothing about information quality; millions of people using a program reflects its seniority, not its quality.
numbers: People "hype watch" an 80,000-view video over an identical 80-view one

title: Question anyone who profits from you
statement: Anyone who profits from a product should have their integrity questioned, even with good intentions; when a creator starts selling to you, start questioning him. Character matters almost as much as content, and integrity means acting on your own stated values.
check: Is the source of the advice free of a financial stake in what he recommends?

title: The red-flag rule
statement: One red flag is a flaw, two means be wary, three means unsubscribe. Flags include 20-inch-arm claims, abs out of proportion with real strength, flip-flopping between bodybuilder and strength-athlete identities, banning critics, and a contrarian "everyone else is wrong" attitude.
numbers: 1 = flaw, 2 = wary, 3 = unsubscribe; his six criteria rule out ~95% of fitness YouTubers
confidence: low — 1 video, 2021 (flags repeated in others to 2024)

title: Test a guru by contradicting him
statement: Politely contradict a guru in his comments and see if he bans you; blocking or refusing to answer is a red flag.

title: Pics or it didn't happen
statement: Unverifiable claims are worthless. Liars go straight for world-record numbers, and progress updates from small, blurry or old photos signal deception.
scope: Lift and physique claims; to disprove fake plates, show, load and pull without cutting the camera

title: Social-media physiques are illusions
statement: Online physiques come from pump, flexing, lighting, best angles, edited thumbnails and the one best shot of hundreds. In his "fitness influencer syndrome", successful influencers stop growing and stay lean to look bigger on camera.
numbers: He says Eubank is ~170 lb but looks bigger than NH

title: YouTubers misreport body fat, height and intake
statement: YouTubers understate body fat and misreport height and calories, so YouTube fitness thinks 17-18% looks obese; influencers use claimed drops to sell.
numbers: Guys at 13-14% claim under 10%; errors often ~5%; real 8% means striations and feathering; example sales claim 18% to 13%

title: A good educator gives keys, not doors
statement: A good educator gives keys but never says which doors to open and reaches people unlike himself. Don't let a teacher own you; you are your own best teacher.

title: "Do your own research" is risky for beginners
statement: For beginners, "do your own research" is Russian roulette, because the algorithm mirrors what you click and feeds them steroid users and teen influencers; many small natural channels give excellent advice.

title: Fake naturals are "killing YouTube fitness"
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: In his view, fake naturals selling transformations, programs and supplements off drug-built physiques are the core rot: they need you to believe training made their size, and you learn nothing from them. Pros on drugs mostly hurt themselves; influencers who juice to sell hurt others, so "their body, their choice" fails once they sell.
status: changed — see IND-43: by 2025 he ranks honest enhanced influencers as the bigger problem

title: Natural viewers, enhanced role models
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: He claims over 99% of fitness viewers are natural while the biggest channels are enhanced, which normalises drug use and leaves young naturals with unrelatable role models, so they get smaller and more discouraged.
numbers: >99% of viewers natural (his estimate)

title: Drop anyone who lies about drugs
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: If someone lies to you about drugs, stop watching; unfollow anyone pushing you toward PEDs. Even so, a natural preacher who secretly lies still keeps you natural.

title: "Just TRT" and "downsizing" are lies
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: He treats "just TRT", "small dose now", "downsizing" and "reached my natural limit" as lies and calls TRT the new YouTube fraud; he claims he can't name one enhanced YouTuber who isn't lying at least a little. Pros who "downsize" were likely warned by doctors and rarely lose size.

title: TRT clinics are profit-driven
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: In his view TRT and youth clinics hook men on high levels, downplay side effects, prescribe to almost anyone who pays and push the age lower; the "low-T modern man" narrative is pushed by those profiting from testing and supplements.
scope: Men considering TRT; the hormone evidence is SCI-42

title: PED "honesty" became promotion
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: PED openness, jokes, memes and "harm reduction" content made PED use mainstream and work as promotion; neutrality effectively sides with PEDs. By 2025 he sees honest enhanced influencers as the main problem, more than fake naturals. He compares it to tobacco and says prevention by preaching works.
status: changed — 2020-2022: fake naturals are the main enemy; 2022-2025: honest enhanced influencers normalising PEDs are the bigger problem

title: PEDs to make money don't pay
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: Taking PEDs to earn from your physique is wrong and doesn't work: most young users never go pro or earn, and many pro-card holders still need side jobs.
scope: Young lifters considering PEDs for a career

title: Naturals shouldn't do business with PED users
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: A natural who promotes natural lifting shouldn't collaborate or do business with PED users, and he never will; naturals who tempt people toward drugs "are not his brothers".

title: Pro bodybuilding is a dying fringe sport
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: Natural bodybuilding is barely represented, enhanced bodybuilding is choking the sport, and pro bodybuilding is a fringe, dying sport of unrelatable freaks watched mostly by non-lifters. He no longer watches the Olympia.

title: Rich Piana as the honest exception
section: PEDs, fake naturals and TRT in the industry
statement: In his view Rich Piana was the one honest PED user, loved because he was open rather than selling lies, and created the "dad" influencer genre; NH believes he had implants.

title: Natty-or-not and call-out videos don't work
statement: They give the target attention and victimhood, feed insecurity, black-pill a generation and benefit only the creator and the subject ("lifters' own tabloids"); starve fake naturals of attention and they fade.
status: changed — 2020: he won't make them but they help newcomers learn natural limits; 2021-2024: they help nobody and "produce nothing good"

title: How natty-or-not grew
statement: He says the format, started around 2014 by Blaha, Vegan Gains, Philion, Doucette and MPMD, grew the biggest channels out of jealousy and greed; PEDs, name-dropping and drama are "the holy trinity of virality".
numbers: ~2014 start; he says Philion went from 40-80 views to over 4M with one video

title: Criticise concepts, not people
statement: Criticise practices and concepts, not people; he asks permission before naming someone in a response video, though published programs and methods are fair game.
scope: Exception: people he considers actively dangerous, covered in "case profile" series backed by screenshots
status: contradicted — he ran long named series on Blaha and Nether Beast (IND-87) and publicly graded dozens of named creators (IND-84); his stated exception is people he thinks dangerous

title: Most fitness YouTube is drama
statement: Most of YouTube fitness is drama and gossip, which is endless, easy and valueless.
numbers: Deleting drama videos would remove ~80% of its content

title: Simple programs, nothing revolutionary
statement: There is no "proven" program and nothing revolutionary: famous novice programs are famous because they're old, programs recombine the same concepts, and good advice is boring. Long science intros and pages of EMG text are fluff.
numbers: A good program fits on a restaurant napkin; he can write one in 25 minutes
check: Can the program's core be written in a few lines (exercises, sets, reps, frequency) without gimmicks?

title: Strip the gimmicks
statement: Most YouTuber programs become decent once the gimmicks are cut; cool names, showy suffering such as 50-rep finishers, and deliberately polarising, contrarian angles are how they're sold.
numbers: Cut about 60% of the gimmicks

title: Constant rotation is a bad sign
statement: Programs that rotate exercises constantly over 16 weeks are rarely well thought out.
numbers: 4 weeks is enough to judge a program

title: YouTube fitness is powerlifting-centric
statement: Much online hypertrophy advice is "strength training wearing a disguise", producing big trunks and legs with afterthought arms; novice programs groom aesthetics-seekers into powerlifters.
numbers: ~75% of the time novices are told to run Starting Strength
scope: Novices who want to look better

title: Powerlifting also brought the good programming
statement: Around 2012 powerlifting brought advice that worked (compound focus, no endless reps, frequency planned for progression), and strength sports gave the platform its good programming principles; even today a medium powerlifting channel gives naturals better size advice than a big bodybuilding channel. Following powerlifters gave him big early progress.

title: No sport owns a movement
statement: Bodybuilders used the big three as long as powerlifters; telling young lifters to do only isolation, or only the big three, is equally wrong. Today's "basics" are just the powerlifting meta (the pullover was once a staple).

title: "Powerbuilding" is a marketing term
statement: "Powerbuilding" means the big three plus lazy isolation sets; compounds plus isolation is just how natural bodybuilders always trained, and most powerbuilders end up poor at both sports. Reclaim the word "bodybuilding".

title: Starting Strength is wrong for bodybuilding
statement: He calls Starting Strength "garbage" for bodybuilding: trainees mostly got fatter, with big legs and a lagging upper body. A program that needs a book to understand is bad, and Rippetoe's "isolation only makes you sore" is nonsense in his view.

title: Programs and sources he rates
statement: He ranks bodybuilding.com (community-vetted) above Reddit above T-Nation, and valued old /fit/ because nobody sold anything. He says Alsruhe's Dark Horse template beats 90% of bodybuilding programs and that his own programming derives from it; 4 Horsemen (by a strongman) is one of the best hypertrophy programs he has reviewed.
numbers: Dark Horse beats 90% of bodybuilding programs; Alsruhe's giant sets: explosive movement, main mover, core, conditioning

title: The pendulum of trends
statement: YouTube fitness swings between extremes: bro bodybuilding then powerlifting, minimalism vs maximalism, science vs anti-science, maingaining vs face-stuffing. The truth sits in the middle, and he wants the pendulum to stop "halfway".
numbers: Minimalism rightly cut fluff ~2011 but kept swinging until it harmed gains

title: Minimalism speaks only to novices
statement: Minimalists ("just do X instead") take away valuable work and only speak to novices; low-maintenance fitness for the lowest common denominator is mediocrity, and "no time" people have time for Netflix.

title: "Functional training" is mostly LARPing
statement: Real athletes and soldiers just call it training or sport-specific training; bodybuilders needn't justify getting bigger, and "useless muscle" talk is propaganda. "Train like an athlete to look like one" is slower than isolating the hypertrophic movement patterns.
scope: Physique goals; functional fitness does get sedentary people moving

title: Suffering is theatre
statement: Exhaustion, screaming, puking, collapsing and burn are theatre or cardio fatigue, not markers of a productive set.

title: Meme myths: fried CNS and fixed set counts
statement: The "fried CNS" meme is nonsense at normal training loads, and fixed weekly-set numbers for naturals are just the new version of the old 8-12 rep myth.
numbers: ~3 h/week of training; set "myths" of 9, 12, 15 or 20 weekly sets

title: Low-rep failure methods repackage HIT
statement: Low-rep-to-failure methods are a softer repackaging of Mentzer's HIT; they work mainly by forcing people who never trained hard to train hard, and promoters use machines because free-weight low reps to failure are hard on tendons. He says Mentzer spread an ineffective method through charisma and looks.
numbers: 4-8 reps to failure

title: Tier lists show their maker's taste
statement: Creators like a lift first and then find reasons, so exercise tier lists download their maker's subjectivity, never match each other and go obsolete.
numbers: Obsolete within about a year

title: Too far toward ultra-stable lifts
statement: Modern hypertrophy culture leans too far toward low-fatigue, ultra-stable lifts; stripping coordination out makes bodybuilding niche and joyless.

title: Evolve, but not for its own sake
statement: Fitness should evolve and tradition or nostalgia aren't arguments, but stay conservative when the new method is worse; staples became popular for a reason.

title: "Science-based" is a marketing label
statement: "Science-based" has become a brand and identity: calling your method optimal claims the high ground and shuts down criticism, "Doctor" titles are arguments from authority, and few of these creators are scientists or read studies well. In his view leaders don't correct their dogmatic fans (he names Israetel's).
numbers: ~1 in 100 viewers read the studies, so it runs on trust
status: changed — 2021: he predicted science channels would lose traction; 2022: Nippard is the best programming channel and this may be the best era for creator quality; 2024: he wants a middle ground, calls Nippard decent and criticises the community's dogmatism (a refinement, not a reversal)

title: Science fear-mongering makes people train less
statement: Fear about fatigue and "optimal" training makes people over-control variables and train less, and promising big extra growth from each new method causes program-hopping; many would have trained more healthily without science content.
numbers: Promises of 30-40% more growth per method

title: Meatheads vs science: each has a strong side
statement: Science has nearly all the logical arguments, meatheads the appealing mindset; each camp has a strong and a weak side, and drama keeps either from wanting the pendulum to stop.
numbers: He frames it as Bugenhagen vs Nippard (2024)

title: Parasocial bonds are harmful
statement: Parasocial relationships with fitness YouTubers rob followers of identity, turn the creator into a father figure and make fans easy to steer into purchases. Loyalty is for family and your dog; watch for your own benefit. Constant positivity hooks dopamine, and he deliberately offends to break the bond.

title: Fanboyism blinds
statement: He likens fanboyism to a mental illness: it blinds followers to lies, makes them swing from total love to total hate, and fanboys never build great physiques because they stop developing themselves.

title: Don't copy idols or hop gurus
statement: Jumping from an exposed guru to his "saviour" is an abusive cycle and only you can save yourself; social media creates "clone wars", and if you clone someone, don't clone him.
numbers: YouTube fitness teaches switching idols every ~6 months

title: Masculinity gurus sell an image
statement: Masculinity and self-improvement gurus sell an image (money, girls, cigars) and test boosters, blame low T or outside factors and keep men frustrated; anyone selling how to be a man is a scam artist. Real masculinity is internal, free and individual, and the spiritual side is left out because it can't be sold.
scope: Men consuming self-improvement content; avoid paid "alpha" content

title: Dogmatism comes from brands
statement: Dogmatism usually comes from a brand that must sell something. Growth takes some dogmatism, because audiences dislike creators who change their minds and novices prefer black-and-white channels.

title: Growth requires clickbait
statement: To grow on fitness YouTube you must clickbait, and most million-subscriber channels lose integrity; he chose to make what he wants and stay small. Titles matter more than thumbnails, and fear thumbnails ("big mistake") force clicks.
numbers: Without clickbait you get ~50k views and the channel dies

title: Entertainment replaced education
statement: YouTube fitness began as informative longer videos and has been taken over by entertainment, Shorts and meme channels; edutainment drifts until entertainment replaces education, and Shorts are almost never informative, though a tutorial short beats a meme short.
numbers: Began ~2009 with 15-20 min videos; now ≤7 min; ~10-20 min is the sweet spot, but pure information is never too long

title: Cut the fitness-content diet
statement: Watching lots of fitness content is information gluttony; the more experienced you are, the less you watch.
numbers: At least 40% of it does nothing for you or harms your mental health; 70% entertainment is wasting your life; he watched ~20 min/week in 2021

title: Novices are the target market
statement: Most fitness content consumers are complete beginners who imprint on the first big channel and form a "renewable pool"; most channels are good for novices, worse for intermediates and useless for advanced lifters, so big channels are gatekeepers to graduate from.
numbers: ~90% of consumers are complete beginners

title: Fitness media is bodybuilding in disguise
statement: Looking better is the most popular online fitness pursuit; CrossFit, Olympic lifting, MMA and calisthenics gained popularity through their athletes' looks.
numbers: ~90% of fitness media is bodybuilding in disguise

title: Comparison content harms self-image
statement: Constant exposure to bigger physiques online worsens self-image, and online genetics talk is used to make the gifted feel superior and others feel bad, never constructively. Many creators stopped progressing to maintain and monetise (some cut and bulk the same ~20 lb yearly), and those who put YouTube over training run out of real knowledge.
numbers: ~20 lb yearly bulk/cut cycle

title: Strength standards aren't objective
statement: Online strength standards are invented from YouTubers' egos ("3 plates in 2 years or you're a loser") or averaged from unfiltered data, so a universal standard fits no one; the honest answer to "when will I have a big chest" is that no one knows.
numbers: One page says a 225 lb bench is standard, another 315 lb

title: Comments are free engagement
statement: Deleting comments or banning critics hurts a channel's reach, and buying subscribers kills its algorithmic standing.

title: Women's fitness is neglected and predatory
section: Women's fitness and the lifting community
statement: YouTube fitness is made for men; women get light "toning" weights, kickbacks and band work, or are told to train like men. Women need their own programming, ideally developed by women, because of different body types, injury tolerance and muscle distribution.
numbers: His female audience ~1-2%; women still told to tone with light weights 30 years later
scope: Women; he notes powerlifting women have the best glutes from heavy squats and deadlifts

title: All lifters should support each other
section: Women's fitness and the lifting community
statement: Bodybuilders, powerlifters, strongmen and calisthenics athletes share a love of iron; swole-shaming and "power copers" who failed at aesthetics poison the community.

title: Fitness should breed above-average people
section: Women's fitness and the lifting community
statement: Fitness is elitist and shouldn't cater to the lowest denominator; body positivity removes agency, except when it gets fat people into the gym.

title: Experienced lifters should teach for free
section: Women's fitness and the lifting community
statement: Experienced lifters should teach newcomers to stay long-term and pass knowledge on for nothing in return.

title: Don't be the form police
section: Women's fitness and the lifting community
statement: Unsolicited form correction rarely helps; only help gym strangers who approach you first.

title: His 200-point channel grading
statement: He grades fitness channels on 20 criteria scored 0-10: 17 core (programming, experience, integrity, usefulness, character, dogmatism, originality, black pill, humor, parasocial, empathy, god complex, production, science, clickbait, recycling, conciseness) plus 3 bonuses (seniority, not selling supplements, physique). Weights are equal although he thinks programming matters more.
numbers: 200 max; graded "French-style", so ~150 is near the practical maximum; scores in the table below

title: Creators he recommends
statement: For programming and size he recommends Nippard (best programming channel in his view, Essentials program), Alsruhe, AlphaDestiny, Schofield, Basement Bodybuilding, Nalewanyj, Israetel/RP for programming and nutrition (not PED advice), Michael Gundill, and Devon Larratt for planning.

title: Creators he criticises
statement: He criticises AthleanX (in his view fake weights and can't program for size), Doucette (integrity 0 in his scoring, extreme standards that black-pill), Humiston, Liver King, MPMD and Huberman (supplement sales), and those he calls the Gymshark "fake natties" of his generation.

title: The "case profile" series on Blaha and Nether Beast
statement: In a long series he alleges that Jason Blaha and Nether Beast faked lifts and plates, invented backgrounds, ran sock accounts and sent copy-paste client programs; these are his allegations, which he says he cross-checks while protecting informants.
numbers: ~25 videos; in 2021 he revised his estimate of Blaha's height to ~5'4"-5'5"; he claims a "three-plate" front squat was two 45s plus a 5 lb bumper
scope: His allegations, unverified; his stated exception to IND-50

title: Your own body is the best evidence
statement: Your own body's data is the most valid evidence; studies are group generalisations that are worthless until tested on yourself, and your experience matters more than his or all the science. "Optimal" is whatever you've proven works on your body.
check: Is the method judged by how the lifter actually responded to it, not only by what studies say?

title: He doesn't cite studies
statement: He never cites or links studies or uses them as arguments of authority; his channel shares experience, and a natural with a good physique is "a mine of knowledge" as valuable as peer review.
status: contradicted — he invokes specific studies when they support him (tempo, ROM, boxers, 500 mg testosterone, lengthened vs 90°), close to the cherry-picking he criticises (SCI-12)

title: You can grow without science
statement: There is a threshold of needed knowledge, mainly technique and form adapted to your body; beyond that, literature is a bonus ("the cherry on top"). Biomechanics are important but learned through training rather than books.
numbers: His first ~5 years ran on bro science and anime

title: Read science only if it improves training
statement: Learning only from your body costs mistakes and possibly gains, so combine both; read science only insofar as it improves your training, and if it takes away from training it's a hindrance.

title: The middle ground: experience ×10
statement: The best approach sits between experience and science; real evidence-based lifting is "experience-based lifting times ten", pooling many people's experience. Good science coaching mixes bro-scientist and real scientist, which is nearly impossible. The science boom triggered an anti-science swing, and both camps strawman each other.

title: The note-taking lifter is a scientist
statement: Someone who trains 10 years, takes notes, learns to program and eats well is more of a scientist than paper-waving YouTubers; for him science means empiricism, and programming is a reproducible science with hard numbers.
numbers: 10 years of training
scope: Experienced lifters, who are "a library" even without papers

title: One observation is not evidence
statement: One person's observation is experience, not evidence: share it, but don't call it scientific. A method working for you doesn't prove it's superior, because novices grow on anything new in a surplus.

title: Bro science is often science not yet proven
statement: Lifters reached many now-accepted guidelines by instinct decades before science backed them; nucleus overload, weighted stretching and lengthened partials were practised before the studies.
numbers: 2-4 sets, 48 h between muscle groups, 7-14 weekly sets, reached 30-40 years before science

title: ~90% has been known for a century
statement: New "optimal" research covers the remaining 10% and mostly confirms the basics; supposed breakthroughs have sat in the literature for decades. Newer studies on volume, tempo, partials and lengthened training are inconclusive and contradictory, which "keeps the content flowing". Studies are best at saying what not to do.
numbers: ~90% known for a century; breakthroughs in the literature ~30 years

title: Simple but not easy
statement: Hypertrophy is simple but not easy and has no hidden secret; if a principle seems complex, it's probably misunderstood. Some aspects, like nucleus overload, are underused.

title: Anti-scientism, not anti-science
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: He opposes what science has become on YouTube ("meme science", scientism), not the scientific method. Scientism means trusting methods so much you stop checking them; "believe in science" is a contradiction because real science is skepticism, and calling critics "anti-science" is a dishonest shield.

title: A study exists for any belief
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: For any belief you can google a supporting study; most people read only the abstract and conclusion, never the methods. Starting from a conclusion and then finding a study is scientism, and nearly every fitness YouTuber cites science only when it agrees with them.
check: Was the study read past the abstract (methods, subjects) and not chosen to confirm a conclusion already held?

title: A paper is an opinion backed by facts
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: A paper must be interpreted, the same statistics can say many things, and findings are true only on a timeline. He gives information as opinion so he can update without staking his identity on a study; science channels silently swap papers without admitting error.
numbers: Most papers taken as gospel will be disproven within ~5 years

title: Industry-funded studies favour their funders
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: Studies funded by food, pharma, supplement, soy, dairy or egg interests reliably favour their funders, and science used to push products becomes marketing; single-compound studies can't validate an untested blend, and sellers twist turkesterone studies knowing buyers won't check.

title: Citing science can be an authority move
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: Citing a paper is itself an argument from authority; linking a paper to end a discussion is anti-speech, and "source?" is usually a dismissal tactic.

title: Too much study-reading paralyses
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: Endless study consumption causes paralysis by analysis and raises "pampered lifters" waiting for the perfect workout; hyping science to novices is detrimental.

title: Science used to win arguments is worthless
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: Using science to win arguments or feel superior makes it worthless; abstract-readers who think they're experts are worse than laymen. When he dismantles a study someone throws at him, the reply is always silence.

title: Strength science isn't hypertrophy science
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: Most exercise science is designed around strength and function; applying it straight to hypertrophy is like a surgeon using veterinary studies. The fitness-fatigue model lumps muscle and CNS together and ignores that bodybuilders needn't peak.

title: Pop science loses substance
section: Scientism and how studies get misused
statement: Popularised science loses substance, a trade worth it only if it serves practitioners; pop-science fitness is "Kellogg's to oatmeal" and removes the work of reaching your own conclusions.

title: Rule 3: credentials
statement: His third trust rule is credentials or diplomas in the field; meeting any one of his three rules (demonstrates now, verifiable past proof, credentials; see IND-24) earns his ear, and all three is best. He respects PhDs but is cooler toward academics who never built muscle.
numbers: 3 rules

title: Knowing means being able to replicate
statement: To know something practical like lifting means being able to replicate it; once drugs are excluded, a natural's physique says something about his methods. Of the two outward signs of authority, social proof proves nothing and evidence the method works is what counts, as you judge an oncologist by patients cured.

title: Science-heavy people are often small
statement: Science-based influencers aren't bigger than experience-based lifters, which weakens their claim to a superior method.
status: contradicted — he also says "being bigger is not an argument" and that a 160 lb person can know more nutrition; partly reconciled by his natural-only qualifier (SCI-21)

title: Judge methods by the physiques they produce
statement: Judge methods by the physiques their programs produce across trainees, not by individual anecdotes.

title: Fringe theories are usually wrong
statement: A fringe theory that denies what most agree on (for example, that volume matters) is most likely wrong; anything that works eventually becomes conventional.
check: Does the method accept the consensus basics (e.g. volume matters) rather than deny them?

title: Volume, intensity and frequency drive growth
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Volume, intensity and frequency sit at the top of his pyramid as the main drivers of hypertrophy; beware anyone who says one of them can be ignored. Tempo is near the bottom for naturals.
check: Does the program explicitly manage volume, intensity and frequency rather than ignore one of them?

title: Growth comes from damage under heavy load
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Resistance training aims at muscle-fibre damage that repairs bigger, and most growth comes from damage under heavy weight.
status: changed — 2020: heavy loads are needed for damage; 2025: rep range is "mostly dead" as long as sets are close to failure (SCI-30)

title: Stretch vs concentric
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Earlier he held that muscle is gained mostly via weighted stretch and that the negative is the key; he now believes the concentric builds more than the eccentric and calls the stretch-focused trend contrarian.
numbers: Earlier ranking: negative-only strongest, negative-then-positive middle, positive-only weakest; later he cites a ~100-man study where ~90° training outgrew lengthened-only
scope: Hypertrophy; he proposes a partner-removes-the-negative experiment
status: changed — 2020-2021: weighted stretch and the negative drive growth, "now backed by studies"; 2023-2024: concentric builds more, lengthened partials help only a little (he cites Milo Wolf). The later view is current.

title: Pump, burn and soreness aren't growth signals
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: The pump comes from fast light reps (fast empty-bar curls pump more than heavy ones), a burn means fast-fibre activation rather than a hypertrophy variable, and soreness isn't correlated with growth. He isn't anti-pump: blood flow may help a little.
check: Is progress judged by strength and load over time rather than by pump, burn or soreness?

title: Metabolic stress and TUT are minor
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Metabolic stress is an accessory at best; time under tension is relevant but too chaotic to be a main principle.
numbers: Metabolic stress maybe 3-4% of progression

title: Rep range and tempo matter little
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Tempos across a wide range gave similar hypertrophy with load adjusted, and the special hypertrophy rep range is "mostly dead", since most ranges work close to failure.
numbers: Tempos of 2-8 s/rep similar
status: changed — 2020: some studies favour heavy weights, mainly because light weights make tonnage hard to accumulate; 2024-2025: rep range and tempo matter little near failure (a refinement)

title: EMG predicts growth poorly
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: EMG and activation data are poor predictors of growth and often misread: EMG shows more chest than lats on chin-ups and more abs on squats than crunches, compound-favouring EMG studies use novices, and over the long term isolation is "king" for body parts. Small per-set differences (sumo vs conventional) still compound over years into visibly different development.
scope: Exercise selection claims based on EMG; he also faults studies equating trap-bar and conventional deadlifts and a box-squat study that used more weight on the box
check: Is the exercise choice justified by more than EMG or activation data?

title: More stretch or activation ≠ more growth
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Better stretch or activation in a study doesn't mean more growth, and researchers chase spicy findings like leg press beating squats.

title: Volume-equated frequency studies are misleading
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: The study showing equal growth at 1x vs 3x/week with volume equated is flawed in his view, because higher frequency lets you accumulate more volume, so volume is never equal in practice.
numbers: 1x vs 3x/week

title: Distrust of "failure is unnecessary" studies
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: He distrusts studies claiming failure is unnecessary, finding their parameters skewed toward the conclusion.

title: Nucleus overload works in his experience
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: High-volume, high-frequency, low-intensity work adds satellite cells and myonuclei in his experience; he doesn't care whether the mechanism is hypertrophy or hyperplasia, only whether the muscle grows. Youth activity may raise myonuclei for life.
scope: Specialisation; in 2022 he attributed it mainly to hyperplasia via metabolic stress (unclear statement)

title: Neural adaptation is a learning phase
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Neural adaptation happens in a learning phase, not over years; once proficient, strength gains come from muscle unless form changes, and joints strengthen far too slowly to explain yearly gains. Past the novice phase, track strength and tonnage as the sign of muscle gain.

title: Muscles don't need shocking
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Muscles don't need confusing or "shocking"; bones, tendons and fibres just respond to the stress placed on them.

title: Range-of-motion data are thin
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Hypertrophy value can't be assigned universally by phase of a lift; it depends on the lift and range of motion, and nobody agrees which lift loads where. ROM/mechanical tension ranks 3rd in his tier list.
numbers: ROM data exist only for hamstrings, biceps and triceps; one study on lifting technique

title: Tier system for training parameters
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: He ranks training parameters S (vital), A (important), B (useful), C (negligible), D (irrelevant or sabotaging); build training from S and A, treat C and D as optional fun. Fast/slow-twitch profiling is D tier: find out in practice which muscles respond to high or low reps.
numbers: 95% of training from S and A, 5% from B, C/D optional

title: Belief changes results
section: What the evidence says about hypertrophy mechanisms
statement: Through placebo, a suboptimal method you believe in can work, and through nocebo a distrusted optimal one can underperform.

title: No body-fat method is accurate
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: No body-fat method is accurate, DEXA included; DEXA can be skewed by water intake, and a scan proves nothing without a baseline. Track strength and tonnage instead.
numbers: In the 15-20% range each percent of error matters a lot

title: PEDs work even without training
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: He cites men on testosterone outgrowing properly training naturals without training themselves, and notes real users take far more for much longer.
numbers: 500 mg/week testosterone in the study; real users take more for 10-20 years
scope: Natural vs enhanced comparisons; see ch. 2

title: Testosterone-decline claims are doubtful
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: Evolution can't halve testosterone in a century, so modern men are biologically like drug-free bodybuilders of 100 years ago; decline studies may reflect poor lifestyles.
numbers: ~100 years; he'd want a study of athletic, whole-food, sober men sleeping 8 h from age 20 to 35+

title: Supplement T-boost data are weak
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: Supplement testosterone data are weak and rat studies are irrelevant; he notes the human figures cited by MPMD for tongkat ali and ashwagandha. A study claiming cricket powder is more digestible than whey mostly showed faster absorption.
numbers: ~30% more free T (tongkat ali), claimed ~50% (ashwagandha), both ~$20; cricket powder "50% more digestible"
scope: T-booster and protein claims; supplements themselves are in ch. 10

title: NoFap and semen retention are myths
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: Testosterone dips briefly after ejaculation then returns to baseline, abstinence gives a brief rise before levels fall back, and feeling horny or aggressive isn't elevated T; boxers' sex before fights doesn't hurt performance.
numbers: T dips ~1 h after ejaculation; ~21 ejaculations/month linked in some studies to lower prostate cancer risk, others disagree

title: Long sessions don't make you catabolic
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: The idea that training past an hour or so turns you catabolic via cortisol is nonsense.

title: Resistance training protects health
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: Longevity correlates with resistance training, it makes bones denser, and exercise doesn't age you.
numbers: Long-time trainees can have ~5x the leg muscle of untrained people

title: Muscle memory is real but not magic
section: Body composition, hormones and health data
statement: Muscle memory speeds regaining lost muscle but isn't magic, and there's no evidence that training while starving "stores" gains for later.
numbers: Perhaps 10 years of work regained in 5-6

title: Build body and mind together
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Body and spirit must be developed together; the ideal is the "complete man" or "educated barbarian". Training without reading and thinking is as unbalanced as theory without a body.
numbers: Training 10 h/day without reading "won't even produce proper gains".
scope: Everyone, especially men; applies to lifters and to intellectuals alike.
status: changed — 2020: the body is "the lesser part", an envelope ("you are not your body"); 2021-23: body and soul are one coin and the body belongs at the centre of life (see PHI-03).
check: Does the program or advice treat training as part of a whole life that also includes reading, thinking and other people?

title: Modern life inverted the mind-body balance
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Modern life is almost all mind and little body, while antiquity was balanced. He blames mind-body dualism (traced to Christianity's view of the body as impure) and schools built to train desk workers, and wants physical education restored.
numbers: ~95% mind / 5% body today vs ~50/50 in antiquity; 2 h of school PE a week is not enough.

title: The body is not a disposable vessel
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Body and soul are two sides of one coin; a mind in an inactive body withers. He cites ancient models: Socrates on citizens having no right to be amateurs in physical training, Plato's name possibly meaning "broad shoulders", Nietzsche's long walks.
status: changed — in 2020 he called the body "the lesser part"; from 2021 he puts it at the centre.

title: Lifting is a Way and a spiritual practice
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Lifting is "iron meditation", a ritual linking you to ancestors who did physical labour, and worship of the body rather than narcissism. Its true value is spiritual; if you are not physically training you are not walking the Way. Bodybuilding has been desacralized.
scope: Lifters; in 2024 he framed his training as worshipping nature.

title: Lifting teaches agency and independence
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Lifting teaches personal responsibility and that hard work pays. It is anti-fragile, anti-consumerist and anti-establishment because strength makes you need institutions less. If everyone lifted, most social problems would shrink; he calls fitness "the most important thing a man can do".
scope: Men in particular; general claim about society.

title: Results without effort can't fulfil you
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Natural lifting builds lasting pride; results bought with a crutch can't fulfil you ("equivalent exchange": results without effort are paid for with lifespan). A big natural body built properly "brings a philosophy with it".
scope: Naturals vs PED users (for the natural/enhanced debate itself, see ch. 2).

title: The gym won't fix your life
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: The milestone you chase (three-plate bench, six-pack) won't make you happy. Muscle is "only a boost" that needs a personality to match, PEDs don't cure insecurity, and social skills matter more day to day.
scope: Everyone; especially men expecting a physique to fix their social or dating life.

title: Fitness should enhance life, not consume it
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Any physical culture is valid if your heart is in it; it doesn't have to be bodybuilding, but every man should be active in some form (lifting, running, swimming). Training ranks below family and work.
numbers: Priorities: family > work > training; skip the gym only for job, studies or family.

title: Discipline spreads to the rest of life
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Discipline and virtue carry over from one area of life to every other, the way a strong squat carries over to every knee-flexion exercise. Lifting has to be experienced; reading about it can't replace doing it.

title: Lifting is Sisyphus, not war
section: Body and mind: the complete man
statement: Meaning, even happiness, comes from repeating the effort ("we freely choose our boulder", after Camus). Framing lifting as war is good motivation but takes the hobby too seriously, since you are not risking your life.

title: Health comes before muscle
statement: Being muscular is pointless if you die in your 50s; sickness takes the muscle anyway. Natural bodybuilding is also about a long life. Great genetics don't excuse neglecting health (he cites Apollon, a lifelong smoker who died young of throat cancer).
numbers: 350 lb isn't healthy even at 6% body fat.
check: Does the approach put long-term health ahead of maximal size?

title: Muscle is your lifeline in old age
statement: People lose the ability to walk without glute, hamstring and quad muscle. He wants to be mobile and strong at 70-80 and keep the ability to squat and hinge heavy, even with less volume and intensity. "We all age but we don't have to get old."
numbers: Lifelong trainees should live healthy to 80-85; dying at 70 is "a tragedy"; mobile and strong at 70-80.

title: Decline comes from inactivity, not age
statement: The age at which people say their body "stopped working" keeps falling; someone who takes care of himself should still thrive at 40, 50, 60 and beyond. Old men who keep their fire share a lifelong passion, physical activity and a family.
numbers: "Body stopped working" age falling from 50s → 40s → 30s → 20s.

title: Spend your energy fully while young
statement: Work hard until 40 because that energy won't reappear at 60; two decades of hard work buy four easier decades with a good body. In old age, accept the contraction: expand like a supernova in your prime, then let wisdom replace strength. Clinging to youth is the neurosis of the old.
numbers: Full effort until 40; 2 decades (20s-30s) of hard work → 4 easier decades.

title: Get regular medical check-ups
statement: Most early male deaths come from ignoring check-ups. Do bloodwork, dentist and general check-ups regularly and start prostate screening on time.
numbers: Bloodwork ~2x/year; prostate screening from the 50s, late 40s for men of African descent (he says their death risk is double); men die ~5 years younger than women.

title: Prevention first, medicine as last resort
statement: He refuses drugs while healthy but would take a pill needed to survive; psychiatric medication is fine as a crutch to start change, not for life. He thinks ADHD is overdiagnosed in energetic boys who need to move. He personally avoids painkillers and won't get LASIK.

title: The dose makes the poison
statement: Stress, training and every good thing become harmful in excess, and some things are harmful even in small amounts. Never being stressed leaves you bored; too much breaks you.
scope: General principle, applied to training load and life stress.

title: Daily health habits
statement: Walk every day in any weather; say out loud on a healthy morning that it is a good day; eat with others and without screens. Break up sitting with short walks; the "sitting kills" study ignored activity.
numbers: Walk 3-4 min every 35-45 min of sitting; 6 h sitting + 2 h training beats a standing desk with no exercise.

title: Breathe through the nose
statement: Breathe in through the nose always, in life and training: it filters germs and warms and humidifies air. "Mewing" is just normal tongue posture with no data that it changes adult faces.

title: Posture has no quick fix
statement: Strengthen traps (face pulls), abs and lower back, use a lumbar pillow, and hold posture deliberately (shoulders back, chin tucked, screens at eye level).

title: Sun, heat and grooming
statement: Build sun tolerance progressively and get some daily; use a sun lamp in gloomy climates; no fake tans; he thinks many sunscreens disrupt hormones, so limit exposure. In heat, gulp water between sets, use a fan, acclimatise and salt for electrolytes. Prefer cold showers and natural soaps.
numbers: Sun 20 → 25 → 30 → 35 min, ~20 min/day; wash hair 2-3x/week; he trains fine at 100 °F.

title: Lifting protects health
statement: Lifting lowers blood pressure and the risk of cancer, diabetes and heart attacks, builds muscle you carry into old age and adds resilience to accidents (neck muscles in a crash). Gaming is catabolic because hours of sitting shrink muscle (his expectation, not studied).

title: Disease impedes the body, not the will
statement: The real damage of illness comes when the mind syncs with the weakened body. Treating mental-health issues as unable to stop your will makes you a tougher opponent for them.

title: Pleasure must follow effort
statement: Pleasure should be the by-product of and reward for effort, never pursued for its own sake. Pleasure is a spike and a valley; happiness is constant. Pleasures not preceded by effort ("eating out of boredom") are toxic.
check: Is the reward (food, rest, leisure) earned by effort rather than pursued for its own sake?

title: Enjoy pleasures without depending on one
statement: Enjoy pleasures on your own terms, but don't make any one of them your only source of happiness, so you can lose it without pain. Stoicism is not mortification.

title: Struggle is necessary
statement: Life works like progressive overload; removing struggle makes people miserable. Struggle breaks you or tempers you. Seek out the "tiger" modernity removed and get things done in the storm rather than waiting for it to pass.

title: Comfort corrodes; improve by subtraction
statement: Self-improvement should mostly mean removing comforts and habits, not adding routines. Society shields people from hardship for decades; he believes we are in the "weak men create hard times" phase. Training against the elements strengthens body and mind.
numbers: Shielded from hardship for the first 25-30 years.

title: Hard work always improves results
statement: Hard work doesn't guarantee winning but always improves results; working hard without working smart is slower and riskier. "No time" is false: we have more free time than ever and spend it on screens.
numbers: ~10 real years of training make a master in any skill; people once exercised ~8 h/day out of necessity.

title: Less effort, less gratitude
statement: The less you work for something, the less grateful you are for it: lottery winners become miserable, spoiling someone removes their reason to strive, participation trophies devalue reward.

title: Don't resign yourself to mediocrity
statement: Giving up has become cool and victim mentality is comfortable; resigning yourself to mediocrity in your 20s means giving up on life. People resent self-improvers because it makes them accountable.

title: The drive is internal
statement: Owning a squat rack doesn't guarantee legs and lacking one doesn't prevent them; don't be limited by preconceived uses of tools.

title: Feed good desires, starve the rest
statement: Desire is not bad; it sets you in motion. Feed desires that are good for you and your community and starve the rest. Trendy renunciation can mask passivity, because ignored desires fester.

title: Contemplate your death daily
statement: Contemplate death every day, as the samurai and Stoics did. Accepting it is "the first day of your real life", removes fear and makes limited time matter; it is not nihilism. Every fear is ultimately fear of death.

title: Avoid death but don't fear it
statement: Keep self-preservation, but fear of death ruins quality of life. "You might die tomorrow anyway" is no way to plan; control what you can. Mortality gives life its flavour, and wanting immortality is childish.

title: Live for convictions you'd die for
statement: A man unwilling to die for his convictions is not willing to live for them. Find the one thing you love enough to accept it killing you. He would die trying to save his family.

title: Grieve without numbing
statement: Grief comes in waves that shrink over time; don't numb it with alcohol, drugs, rebounds or partying. Grief is the price of love and always worth it, so spend time with your living parents.

title: Fame is worthless; impact counts
statement: Judge success by your positive impact on others, even if nobody credits you. You take nothing to the grave except that impact. Early fame derails people.

title: Believe in free will completely
statement: There is no destiny; bad genes and an external locus of control are excuses. Believing in total free will is "naive but brave", believing you have none is cowardly. Life is poker: play the hand you're dealt.

title: Uprightness is a choice
statement: Environment makes being upright easier or harder but never impossible; worth comes from what you pursue, not birth. Being smart and having gym drive depend more on education and environment than on birth.

title: Responsibility makes you an adult
statement: Accepting responsibility is what makes you an adult; avoiding it produces Peter Pan (puer aeternus) men. Becoming a man takes work and a journey out into the world.

title: Events are neutral; control the present
statement: Your opinion of events causes the suffering. Only the present can be controlled, so don't lament the past or worry about fate or one-in-a-million events. Rehearse realistic scenarios once, then let them go.

title: Own your feelings toward others
statement: Negative feelings toward people are within your control; blaming others for them escapes responsibility. Blaming the system for failures while claiming credit for successes is pathetic.

title: Build your identity alone first
statement: Build yourself through many uncomfortable hours of solitude, then return to the group as an asset. Don't stay a permanent hermit or "sigma". "Become your own best friend."
scope: Young people especially; time alone as a teen is a sound investment.

title: Strong individuals make strong collectives
statement: Individualism is not selfishness: you build yourself in order to be useful. His balance sits closer to the individualistic side; the isolated lone wolf becomes pathological, and healthy masculinity is community-driven.

title: Group identity is a comfortable trap
statement: A group identity is borrowed and comfortable, and that comfort is the trap. A healthy group lets you exist outside it and leave; leave any group that does nothing for you. Cults use love bombing and constant activity.

title: Don't tie identity to anything you can lose
statement: Don't tie your identity to a job, possessions, a belief, sobriety, a diagnosis or a trauma. Losing them would crush you, a trauma made into identity can't heal, and a belief that became identity is almost impossible to correct.

title: Walk your own path
statement: Never hand your free will to another man: your own worst decisions about your life beat someone else's best. Don't worship anyone, NH included. Decide what you want before self-improvement, or you'll copy influencers' goals.

title: The self is built, never finished
statement: The true self is built, not found, and development ends only at death. Later framed as Jungian individuation, with the self ruling the ego.
numbers: Every 5 years you should look back and see you were an idiot.

title: Wear masks, don't become them
statement: Wear a social mask when needed, especially at work or in academia, but never let it become you. Outsiders should learn what makes "normies" tick. True love only blossoms when both partners drop their masks.
status: contradicted — "be frank and sincere" vs "be a closed book" and keep a "secret garden" from his wife; partly reconciled by this mask doctrine.

title: Ignore the crabs in the bucket
statement: Anyone with a real goal meets people who pull them down because success removes their excuses; set sail anyway and surround yourself with go-getters. Hiding your accomplishments only keeps others comfortable in mediocrity.

title: Change your environment to change yourself
statement: Changing your environment is one of the few real ways to change yourself. Leaving home alone to study in the US "made him a man", and he thinks every young man needs something similar.
numbers: He left home at 20.

title: Kindness only counts from the strong
statement: Kindness is a virtue only in someone who could be a tyrant. Become strong, then choose to be kind; a weak person's niceness is camouflaged cowardice. "Kind without strong is weakness, strong without kind is useless."
check: Is strength framed as something to put at the service of others rather than an end in itself?

title: Masculinity is contained strength in service
statement: Healthy masculinity is great strength contained and put at the service of others, especially the weak: a dog with a wolf's power, never a sheep. By 2025 he defines masculinity as essentially providing service.

title: "Toxic masculinity" is imbalance
statement: Toxic masculinity is too little or too much, not masculinity itself. Only masculinity can stop masculine violence, so don't amputate its dark side; refine natural aggression into protection. Masculinity is shield and sword.

title: A man is made, not born
statement: Masculinity is rooted in hormones but needs culture, oral tradition and rites of passage. France abolished military service and has no rite of passage left, so men stay boys.
numbers: Viking boys had to survive 15 winters, ride, hunt and build.

title: Masculinity can't be bought
statement: Masculinity is internal and free. Fitness products, supermarket meat, guns and hyper-masculine personas only sell an imitation.

title: Fatherless society; learn from family men
statement: Young men without role models fall for hyper-masculine online caricatures and gurus with no lasting families. Take advice from older men with families; raising kids and building something is manlier than glorified dying young.

title: Men need the whole emotional range
statement: Being a man includes crying and grief. Emotional concealment is "the number one reason" men are not doing well, and repressed emotion explodes onto loved ones. Male loneliness is real.
status: contradicted — he also observes (a friend dumped two days after crying) that sad men get treated "like a broken tool"; descriptive vs normative, never fully reconciled.

title: Reclaim anger that fuels the will
statement: Modern men are over-domesticated and need their fire back. Embrace anger if it fuels your will without letting it consume you; Stoic anti-anger suited fiery ancient men, not soft modern ones. An angry look is a social warning that prevents violence.
status: changed — 2020: leave aggression at the gym, wrath is a capital sin, repress urges in your 20s; 2022-24: experience and channel anger and emotion rather than suppress them.

title: Self-declared alphas aren't alphas
statement: Alphas take position by force but keep it through care and example; alpha/sigma typologies are "astrology for men". Hierarchies are social and mobile.

title: Real pride is internal
statement: Healthy pride is closer to narcissism than society admits, but boasting unprompted shows insecurity; true experts don't announce it. Pride becomes arrogance when you stop learning or crush others.

title: Independence and self-sufficiency
statement: Independence is a core male quality: refuse handouts, which he calls traps, because men are treated as expendable. A grown man cooks, cleans and does his own laundry; a 28-year-old who can't cook is "pathetic".

title: Every man should be able to defend himself
statement: Violence is neutral and part of life; believing you'll never face it is childish. If good men are pacified, no one stops the bad ("si vis pacem para bellum"). Martial arts can be a door into physical culture.

title: Self-defence rules
statement: Fight back rather than submit; never follow an attacker to a second location; in a mugging, don't show fear or pretend nothing is happening. If followed, stay in light and among people. Aggressors look for prey that won't resist.

title: Suppressed violence turns psychological
statement: Suppressed physical violence becomes psychological violence and passive aggression, which he calls worse than open confrontation. Bullies only stop when met with matching force, and zero-tolerance policies make bullying worse; don't become a bully after being bullied.

title: Strict boundaries get respected
statement: Most people are neutral; your weakness turns them into jerks. Predators sense weakness, and boundary-pushers are cowards who stop when called out. Women must be twice as strict because they lack physical strength to back boundaries up.

title: Never hit a woman except to protect life
statement: Never hit a woman except to protect a life; if constant nagging becomes psychological violence, leave.

title: "Man vs bear" statistics he cited
statement: He cited figures he says show men are far more violent than women but also most homicide victims themselves, and recommends women read *The Gift of Fear*.
numbers: ~80% of murder victims are men; men commit ~80% of homicides; ~9 in 10 femicides by a known man, ~60% partners; US women 2020: ~300,000 heart-disease deaths, 10,000 car deaths, ~3,000 murders; bears kill ~1-6 people/year in North America.

title: Lifting won't make you a fighter
statement: Fighting is mostly skill. To fight better, train fighting; lifting only complements it. Yet the idea that weights make fighters slow is a myth holding back karate and judo coaches.
numbers: 10 years of gym training loses to 2 years of boxing or BJJ; a BJJ blue belt would beat him even at +50 lb.
scope: Lifters who want to fight; martial artists.
status: contradicted — weights making fighters slow is "a myth", but in the same video big enhanced bodybuilders are slow and gas out (likely extreme size vs moderate lifting, not reconciled).
check: Does a fighter's plan put fight training ahead of lifting?

title: Max size and max skill don't mix
statement: You can't be maximally big and maximally athletic or skilled. BJJ in particular is so time-consuming that non-novices can't keep growing muscle.

title: Strike power comes from the hips
statement: Strikes are powered by hip rotation with feet planted, not the arm; being big doesn't guarantee winning. A 500 lb box squat has little to do with kick power, flying kicks are rare in real fights, and a punching tower that blocks hip rotation has no carryover.

title: Street arts and combining with lifting
statement: For the street: baseline striking plus some wrestling (boxing, savate, muay thai); avoid ground arts there. When starting kickboxing, combine it with lifting, ease in, then shift energy toward it. Wrestling is itself resistance training.
numbers: Boxing/savate template: 2 lifting days + 1 conditioning day/week; kickboxing 2x/week, lift the day after (garbled).
scope: Martial artists, beginners in combat sports.
status: contradicted — mild: he likes grappling above all and practised judo (2020) but advises avoiding ground arts for the street (2024); different contexts.

title: Athletes: sport first, then gym
statement: Priority: play the sport, then drills, then hypertrophy. Athletes need minimal programs that carry over; weight training builds injury resilience and strength but is never as specific as practice. Keep some gym work in season and test speed and agility regularly. Mention outside sports when submitting a program.
numbers: In season: keep 2-3 h/week of gym work.
scope: Athletes; martial artists need less lifting volume (trap bar deadlifts suit them).

title: Question morality; judge by consequences
statement: Morality is man-made, so question it constantly and judge morals, people and theories by consequences, not intentions. A toxic morality must be fixed, not abolished; judge one by whether you can live with its consequences (amor fati).
status: changed — 2021 Stoic cycle: virtue is built into nature and immortal; 2022+: morality is man-made and judged by consequences (already in 2020 he said good and evil don't exist in nature but are socially useful).

title: Master versus slave morality
statement: The weak invert values so the strong become "evil", and victimhood becomes the moral weapon of those who can't win on argument. Nietzsche's answer is to get strong yourself. Swole-shaming follows the same logic.

title: Whatever expands you is good
statement: Will to power is the never-satisfied drive to expand, not "big muscles or being an alpha". Growing embraces life; shrinking from pain leads toward depression. The Übermensch creates his own values but doesn't reject morality, and is an unreachable ideal; unlike Nietzsche, NH thinks everyone can break their conditioning.

title: Nietzsche is misread
statement: Nietzsche was not a relativist, anti-religion or a nihilist; he questioned morals rather than abolishing them, and "God is dead" was a diagnosis, not a celebration.

title: Virtue is costly action, not signalling
statement: Virtue is internal and shows in costly action; those who advertise their goodness usually lack it. Tolerance is passive and costs nothing, and being nice is not a virtue. Naturals who stay natural are simply living the virtue.

title: Lead by example, not preaching
statement: Virtue is taught by example; proselytising never works. A good father lets his kids see him train and treats their mother tenderly.

title: Do good without seeking reward
statement: Chasing kickbacks corrupts you and helping for interest is impure. He treats money lent to friends as gone and gives rather than lends.

title: Hold a few firm principles
statement: Hold a few firm principles even against the majority; moral relativism produces spineless people who can be sold anything, and a principle dropped when inconvenient was never yours. Nuancing a belief over time is adapting, not flip-flopping. He refuses ads and sponsorships on principle.

title: Vice is a parasite
statement: Vice is a parasite, not who you are; reject it in yourself rather than flee it in others. Lust and greed top his ranking of sins because most people suffer from one or the other. Vice and virtue are contagious.

title: High standards and earned hierarchy
statement: He defends elitism: high standards create excellent people and inequality drove humans to strive. Healthy hierarchies are earned, unfair ones collapse; equality is a man-made construct, dangerous when mistaken for nature. Shun obesity, smoking and drugs but help people overcome them with compassion.

title: Be sincere and keep your promises
statement: Be sincere and frank; he refuses to lie because tracking lies is too tiring. Keep your promises, to yourself first; the test is whether you can look at yourself in the mirror. Small protective lies exist in every relationship.
status: contradicted — vs "be a closed book" and a "secret garden" from his wife (see PHI-49).

title: No forgiveness without an apology
statement: Everyone deserves a second chance on two conditions: they ask for it and they make an effort.

title: Stoicism is controlled emotion, not coldness
statement: Properly understood, Stoicism means feeling emotion and controlling it, living as an exemplary citizen, and applying it all day. Acceptance applies only to the truly unavoidable; many self-described stoics are smug misreaders.

title: Stoicism is a starter, not the answer
statement: Stoicism is a self-imposed tyranny that passionate ancient men built to tame their chaos; its contempt for the body is wrong and online Stoicism is dogmatic. It remains his recommended entry point. He admits he couldn't apply Stoic indifference to losing his family.
status: changed — 2020: the philosophy he most identifies with; 2021: "not a Stoic", moved to Nietzsche and Jung; 2022-23: it "shames instincts"; 2024: still the recommended starting point, critically qualified.

title: Philosophy must be applied
statement: Unapplied philosophy is "mental masturbation", like collecting gym equipment and never training, and it can poison you by making you feel smart. Never call yourself a philosopher or a stoic; a few short precepts beat volumes of theory.

title: Read widely, not one book
statement: Good philosophies complete each other; read those that make you angry. If one book represents you completely, you are basic. Specialisation pays in fitness but not in intellect.

title: His reading method
statement: Read the book yourself before hearing his take. Read once for style, reread chapter by chapter with a pen, then write a summary; if you can teach it, you understand it. With little time, read first thing in the morning and before bed.
numbers: He reads 12-15 h/week and rereads a book at least 5 times before presenting it.

title: Reading order he recommends
statement: Start with the Stoics (*Meditations* → *Enchiridion* → Seneca's *On the Happy Life* → Epictetus' *Discourses*), not Mishima; then Nietzsche (start with *Beyond Good and Evil*), Jung and Dostoevsky. Early picks: *Book of Five Rings*, *Hagakure*. Others: Adler, *The Gift of Fear*, Campbell, Debord, *48 Laws of Power* "if only to resist manipulation".
numbers: Stoic collection ~$9, ~2 weeks to read; Nietzsche/Jung/Dostoevsky cycle 2+ years.

title: Teach by giving keys
statement: Teach by giving keys, not answers. If you can't explain something clearly you don't understand it, and hoarded knowledge is worthless. A good teacher is a perpetual student, patient, and aims to be surpassed.

title: Musashi and Bushido ideas he keeps
statement: Be able to state your Way of life without hesitating; know one thing deeply and you know ten thousand; rhythm matters more than speed; practise peripheral awareness; think 15 years ahead (Hagakure).
numbers: Plan 15 years ahead.

title: No absolute truth, keep seeking it
statement: Nobody is objective ("objectivity is subjectivity enough people agree on"); accept your subjectivity but keep pursuing objectivity. Whoever controls the media mass-produces "truth".

title: Seek out opposing ideas
statement: Question what society agrees on and seek opposing ideas with egos out of the debate; disagreement creates knowledge, echo chambers create fanboys. A theory is worth something only if it can be refuted. Don't blindly worship scientific authority.

title: Stupidity is refusing to change your mind
statement: Stupidity is refusing to change your mind, not ignorance. Be intelligent rather than appear so; emotional intelligence can matter more than IQ.

title: Ignore the intellectually dishonest
statement: Don't engage the intellectually dishonest; an insult needs your permission to hurt. Online meanness reveals the writer's insecurity. Criticise ideas, not names.

title: Study influence to resist it
statement: Study how influence works so you can't be manipulated; being pigeonholed in one ideology makes you easy prey. People only change when they think the idea is theirs. Manipulation is "the strength of the weak".

title: Cut your news intake
statement: Stop consuming so much news and chatter, especially political content on social media, which persuades you that you have enemies. Constant information makes people miserable.

title: His own religious stance
statement: He moved from baptised, non-practising Catholic to "agnostic but spiritual". He was influenced by Catholicism, Sunni Islam and nature; he studied Islam at 15-16 but couldn't accept giving up free will. When he prays he gives thanks rather than asks.
status: changed — 2020-22: Christian, follows the New Testament his own way; 2024-25: "not religious but spiritual", agnostic.

title: Judge religion by what it builds
statement: Judge a religion by how it structures society and lives, not literal truth. Believing in something beats believing in nothing. Science explains the material world, religion the spiritual, and humans need both; viewers with faith should join a congregation.

title: Faith needs sacrifice and gratitude
statement: Faith without pain or sacrifice is empty and watered-down religion is a shell. Real faith rests on gratitude, not fear.

title: The West lost faith, kept new gods
statement: Religion was mankind's "refinery" that tamed barbarians into chivalrous men. The modern West kept Christian morality but dropped the faith, so money, science, celebrities and hedonism became new gods; most modern neuroses come from a lack of spirituality.

title: Read scripture as allegory
statement: Read religious texts as allegory judged by the norms of their time; following any text to the letter is impossible and unwise. Be wary of religions promising a better afterlife, since it stops people improving on earth.

title: Integrate your shadow
statement: Every man has demons; acknowledge the shadow, integrate it and keep a grip on it, because denying it makes it get loose. Lifting is one way to integrate it. Left too long, it petrifies, and no book can do shadow work for you.

title: The psyche self-regulates
statement: Conscious and unconscious must stay balanced, like blood sugar; dreams and neuroses compensate for a one-sided conscious attitude. Productivity culture overvalues the conscious mind.

title: Keep a dream journal
statement: Keep paper by the bed and write dreams on waking, because the conscious mind erases them within minutes. An interpretation is valid if it resonates with the dreamer and gets them unstuck; a therapist who tells you what your dream means is a bad one.

title: Become your own analyst
statement: Choose a therapist who gives action items, avoids rushing to pills and doesn't feed transference; talk without action is spiralling. Speak about what festers (suicidal thoughts, jealousy, resentment), since speaking takes its power away; euphemisms push it into the unconscious.
scope: Everyone; if a bad childhood doesn't weigh on you, don't dig.

title: Loss of meaning is today's neurosis
statement: Loss of meaning is the general neurosis of our time; spiritual death usually precedes suicide.
numbers: About a third of Jung's patients suffered from emptiness despite material comfort.

title: Happiness is a choice made now
statement: Deferring happiness until a goal is reached leaves you just as miserable; shrink the list of things you need. Progress toward happiness is slow and noticed in hindsight, like lifting.

title: Gratitude is a daily habit
statement: Gratitude separates the wise from fools; it is an active daily habit, not a feeling. Be grateful every day if you were born in the first world.

title: Find a purpose; the ultimate one is love
